steps.text: NA-0753 (R376/R377): the flight-fixes tripwires plus the first LIFECYCLE-shaped coverage. Three launches: configure and arm, drive the armed wipe through the real unlock UI, then relaunch onto the wiped profile and prove the prior relay address did not survive.
na0753-fi-passphrase
na0753-fi-passphrase

X2 arm 1 - the ONBOARDING surface renders the verification code in six 5-digit groups (v2 item 2 as ruled at R377 section 1: one text node, group-boundary wrap left to fitCode). The VALUE is generated fresh each run, so the harness pins SHAPE; the raw 30 digits stay pinned by the Rust value tests.
FI
X2 arm 2 - the SETTINGS surface carries the same grouped form, and both surfaces still agree character for character.

SETTLE, and the reason. Opening the pane calls refreshServerPane(), which is ASYNC: it clears the error and then, AFTER awaiting refreshServerState(), assigns #relay-url.value = savedRelayUrl. The pane className flips SYNCHRONOUSLY, so waiting on it alone races - typing lands first and the in-flight refresh then wipes both the field and any message. Measured: field and error both empty while a probe proved the gate had set them. RE-AIMED BY NA-0754: this row waited on #relay-token-help, which that lane REMOVED along with the other per-field helper sentences. The replacement is #relay-ca-path.placeholder, and it is a STRONGER signal for the same reason the old one worked - renderFieldState() writes it at the very END of refreshServerState(). It is also a REAL transition: the placeholder attribute was deleted from index.html so JS owns it outright, which means it is empty until the async refresh completes and cannot pass before the pane has settled. An attribute present in the markup from the first byte could never have signalled anything.

INSTRUMENT NOTE: the two gate messages are read with prop_eq on textContent, not read_text. read_text polls but is VISIBILITY-COUPLED (WebDriver returns rendered text, empty for an element out of view), and #relay-url-error sits below the fold in a long pane - measured empty by a probe while the message was demonstrably set. prop_eq both POLLS and reads a PROPERTY, so it is race-free AND hidden-safe. NA-0752 moved read_tc -> read_text because read_tc does not poll; this is the same trade from the other side.

X3 arm 1 - THE INTEGER-IP TRAP. https://1234 is ACCEPTED by the engine (Url::parse reads an all-digit host as a packed IPv4 and returns 0.0.4.210 - route.rs:50-74, driven at STOP 1, filed as ENG-0218). The gate refuses it BEFORE any invoke, so no test fires and the field is left byte-identical to what was typed.
https://1234

steps.expect: That's a number, not a server name. Type the address your relay operator gave you, for example https://relay.example.org:8443

steps.text: X3 arm 2 - the missing port is NAMED, not guessed.
https://relay.example.test
X3 arm 3 - the omitted scheme is prepended https (never http) and the prepend is VISIBLE in the field before any test; a dotless LAN-style host with an explicit port is accepted and committed.
relay.example.test:8443
Arm the erase-after-N consequence at the documented minimum of 1, so ONE wrong attempt reaches the limit and the free-tier delay ladder (two free tries) never engages.

SETTLE the vault pane the same way, then ARM. Arm is gated on an explicit acknowledgement checkbox (#wipe-ack, main.js:854) - without it the handler returns early with an inline error and the arm SILENTLY does not happen, which is exactly how this scenario first failed: the wipe never fired because nothing was armed. The armed state is ASSERTED, never assumed.
The arm TOOK: renderWipeState hides Arm and reveals Disarm (main.js:806-807), and the status line names the limit and the remaining count.
Launch 2 on the persisted, configured, ARMED profile: boot lands scr-unlock. One wrong passphrase reaches the armed limit and the vault is wiped.
definitely-wrong-pass

X1 THROUGH THE REAL UI - the app-level residue. Before NA-0753 the armed wipe removed vault.qsv ONLY: qsc owns just its own directory (correct by design), and the desktop's Wiped arm did no app-level cleanup, so settings.json survived carrying the prior profile's relay address and alias. That is the operator's first-flight ghost, and ENG-0048's binding rule failing on the one path its remedy never covered.
Launch 3 - the FRESH-RESTART half. The wiped profile boots as a brand-new install, and the prior relay address is gone from the surface as well as from disk.
